key: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me.
s: Having told the Prophet to turn away yet warn, God speaks in the first person; al-Tabari, on 51:56 to 51:57, takes them, with Ibn Abbas, as made to worship and bow to Him, since deniers too yield to His decree, resisting only His bidding.

evidence.words: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرنا عن ابن عباس، وهو: ما خلقت الجنّ والإنس إلا لعبادتنا، والتذلل لأمرنا. فإن قال قائل: فكيف كفروا وقد خلقهم للتذلل لأمره؟ قيل: إنهم قد تذللوا لقضائه الذي قضاه عليهم، لأن قضاءه جار عليهم، لا يقدرون من الامتناع منه إذا نزل بهم، وإنما خالفه من كفر به في العمل بما أمره به
evidence.gloss: The more correct of the two readings is the one we cited from Ibn Abbas, namely: I created the jinn and humankind only to worship Us and to humble themselves to Our command. If someone asks: how then did they disbelieve, when He created them to humble themselves to His command? It is answered: they have humbled themselves to His decree which He decreed upon them, since His decree runs over them and they cannot hold out against it when it befalls them; the one who disbelieved in Him opposed Him only in acting on what He commanded him.

reason: The problem holds: the sentence gave both halves of al-Tabari’s distinction as ‘command’ (humble themselves before His command; defy only His commands), a paradox on the page. Re-opened al-Tabari on 51:56 to 51:57: he prefers Ibn Abbas’s reading (created for Our worship and humbling to Our amr), then answers the objection by separating His decree (qada’, which the deniers cannot refuse and to which they submit) from acting on what He commanded (ma amarahu bihi, which the denier opposes). Rewrote only the reading so the two terms differ: made to worship and bow to Him, since deniers too yield to His decree, resisting only His bidding. The critic’s longer wording ran to 50 words, over the 45 cap, so the same sense is given in fewer words. Key verse, place, commentator and plain sense unchanged. verse.js ok (Adh-Dhariyat 51:56, at 4730); 44 words; entry-check ok.
